correctness.rationale: Exact root-of-unity filters for weight mod three determine the conditional one- and two-coordinate Fourier moments. Three invariant Gram sectors exhaust dimension 2d+1. Explicit closed rational/radical spectral evaluations yield unique best radius for both parities, with strict positive comparison polynomials and boundary denominator checks. Direct complex Fourier matrix diagonalization was run for d=4..8 and the 463-assertion checker independently corroborated the formulas through d=44; finite tests do not constitute the proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected spherical restriction/extension papers optimize different Lp-to-Lr norms. Published one-Hamming-shell Fourier spectra do not state the kernel or sharp spectral conditioning of the mod-three Hamming-weight unions, and a split quadratic cone in separate coordinate variables is not the same Fourier aperture. Search and full-text implications do not identify an exact stronger covering parity law. Priority risk remains for unindexed association-scheme/Krawtchouk equivalents.
residual_risks: The unindexed classical association-scheme literature may contain equivalent eigenvalue computations or an unrecognized radius optimization theorem.

Published single-shell spectral formulas supply standard ingredients, and a further derivation might possibly extract part of the result without being explicitly stated. Absolute novelty is not certified.

value.rationale: Exact stable reconstruction by a natural low-bandwidth Fourier space from each of three complete ternary quadratic hypersurfaces is a motivated design objective; the parity-switching strict optimal radius and sharp singular-value condition number for all d>=4 are substantive selection rules. The one exceptional singular case and the two-level even-dimensional optimal spectrum delimit the phenomenon. It does not claim broad extension exponents or general fields.
